title: Lavorano per Guess, Calvin Klein, e Tommy Hilfiger, ma guadagnano meno di 1 dollaro al giorno
description: Il settore tessile in Etiopia – il secondo paese più popoloso dell’Africa con 105 milioni di abitanti - cresce a ritmi significativi. Il governo prevede che le esportazioni del comparto, che attualmente valgono 145 milioni di dollari l'anno, salgano a circa 30 miliardi. Un obiettivo tuttavia che appare irrealistico, se non altro perché bassi salari hanno portato a una scarsa produttività, a ripetuti scioperi e a un esasperato turn over (le fabbriche sostituiscono in media tutti i loro dipendenti ogni dodici mesi). Secondo un rapporto della New York University, i lavoratori etiopi con 26 dollari al mese sono tra i meno retribuiti al mondo. E, paradossalmente, sono dipendenti di marchi globali come Guess, H&M, Calvin Klein, Gap, Tommy Hilfiger, e JC Penney che nel paese africano hanno delocalizzato i loro stabilimenti. L'Etiopia, che mira a diventare il principale centro manifatturiero del continente, ha sedotto gli investitori facendo passare il messaggio che sarebbe stato sufficiente riconoscere ai lavoratori meno di un terzo dei salari offerti in Bangladesh. E si consideri che per lo stesso lavoro i kenyoti sono pagati 207 dollari al mese e i cinesi 326.

title: AI Automation Consultant
description: We build and run software that schedules work crews, texts them their jobs, and handles what they get paid. It runs live every day for real businesses. If it breaks, real people don't get told where to go, and real money goes to the wrong place. An AI writes most of the code. We need someone to decide what gets built, and to catch the AI when it gets it wrong -- because it does, and it always sounds confident. What we pay $1,000 a month to start. We review it after your first few weeks, and again once you've shown what you can do. The step up from this job is Client Lead -- you'd run a client on your own and be the person they talk to. It pays significantly more, and we fill it by promoting someone who's already doing this job well. That's where this role is meant to lead. What you'll do Take a vague complaint -- "the schedule is wrong sometimes" -- and work out what's actually happening before changing anything. Write down what a new feature should do, and just as importantly what it should not do, before any code is written. Use the AI to build it, then check its work properly. Read the code like someone is trying to slip something past you. Test on real data with the feature switched off, then switch it on and watch. Nothing goes straight to texting a hundred people. When something breaks: stop the damage, find everything affected, then fix the cause -- not just the one thing that got reported. Write short, clear updates. Most days that's how your team knows what's going on. Who does well here You've built something real. One thing is enough. Something messy, that other people ended up depending on. We'd rather hear about that than a list of technologies. You don't take "it works" for an answer. A passing test and a green dashboard don't settle it for you. You go and check. You think about what happens when things go wrong -- bad input, the same job running twice, someone in a different timezone, a message that says "sent" but never arrived. You're fine saying "I don't know yet, here's how I'd find out." You don't need a degree, a particular language, or years of experience. You do need good judgment, and we test for that directly instead of guessing from your CV. This isn't for you if you want tickets handed to you with the thinking already done, or if you'd ship the AI's first answer because it looked right. How to apply https://volt-os-production-4bc9.up.railway.app/apply Fill in a short form, verify who you are with Telegram, and a 20-minute timed test starts straight away. Do it when you have twenty quiet minutes and decent internet -- you only get one go at it. In the form, tell us about one thing you built that mattered. What was unclear at the start, what you got wrong, and how you found out. That's the part we read closely. What happens after Timed test -- arithmetic, patterns, following written instructions (20 min) Written questions about real situations from the system (~2 hrs) A repo with a bad change hidden in it, and some unfamiliar code to get into (~4-5 hrs) A conversation -- real problems, out loud (~2 hrs) Paid trial, real work, everything reviewed (2-4 weeks) Steps 1-4 are unpaid. The trial is paid from your first day. Most people don't get past step 3. That's expected -- the whole job is about holding a high bar, so we'd rather find out early than three months in. If you need something changed to take this fairly -- extra time, a screen reader, a different format -- just tell us before you start. Asking costs you nothing and isn't part of the test.

With a commitment to providing innovative banking solutions and exceptional customer service, we are expanding our global presence and are seeking a dedicated Officer for our Representative Office in Ethiopia. Job Summary The Officer of the Representative Office will serve as the primary point of contact for the bank’s operations in Ethiopia. This role involves supporting the bank’s strategic initiatives, maintaining relationships with local stakeholders, and promoting the bank’s products and services. The ideal candidate will be knowledgeable about the banking industry and possess strong organizational and communication skills. He/she will be based in Addis Ababa representative office and will fly to Djibouti regularly (minimum 5/6 times a year). Establish and maintain relationships with regulatory authorities, local banks and businesses, and stakeholders. Conduct market research to identify opportunities for the bank’s growth in the region. Coordinate with different departments within the bank to ensure all operations comply with local regulations. Assist in the development and execution of marketing strategies to enhance brand visibility in the Ethiopian market. Prepare and submit periodic reports on market conditions, competitive landscape, and business opportunities to headquarters. Support the onboarding process of local clients and liaise with them to provide exceptional service. Ensure compliance with local laws and regulations related to banking operations and represent the bank in compliance matters. Qualifications Master’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum of 10 years’ experience in banking, trade finance , preferably with some experience in representative or liaison roles. Strong understanding of the banking environment in Ethiopia. Excellent interpersonal and networking skills. Proficiency in both English and French (Amharic and other local languages are a plus). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks effectively. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and familiar with banking software. What We Offer Competitive salary Opportunities for professional growth and development. A dynamic and supportive work environment. Chance to contribute to the growth of a regional banking institution. description: Facebook Instagram Youtube Bushulo Gesundheitszentrum Du engagierst dich gerne sozial und möchtest dich im Gesundheitsbereich einbringen? Dann bist du hier genau richtig! Äthiopien ist ein faszinierendes Land voller Gegensätze: über 80 ethnische Gruppen und ebenso viele Sprachen, über 4.500 m hohe Berge und Absenkungen unter dem Meeresspiegel. Armut, Nahrungsmittelknappheit, häufige Überschwemmungen. Viele Menschen können nicht lesen oder schreiben, sind nicht in die moderne Ökonomie eingebunden und haben nur unzureichenden Zugang zu medizinischer Versorgung. In Äthiopien sterben heute noch immer 353 Frauen auf 100.000 Lebendgeburten. Das ist weit entfernt vom Ziel der Vereinten Nationen, die Müttersterblichkeit auf unter 70 je 100.000 Lebendgeburten zu senken (SDG 3.1)2. Nur zum Vergleich: Die Müttersterblichkeit liegt in Österreich bei 4 Todesfällen je 100.000 Lebendgeburten. Die Sterblichkeitsrate von Kindern unter 5 Jahren liegt in Äthiopien bei 53/1000. In Österreich liegt diese bei 3.6/1000 und die SDGs setzen sich zum Ziel, die vermeidbaren Todesfälle von Kindern unter 5 Jahren in allen Ländern auf maximal 25 Todesfälle pro 1000 Kindern zu senken (SDG 3.2). Einsatzstelle Das Bushulo Gesundheitszentrum wurde 1979 von der Katholischen Kirche Hawassas gegründet und wird von der Ordensgemeinschaft der Franciscan Missionaries of Mary geführt. Über die Programme Safe Motherhood und Ambulanzen der Hoffnung werden die Frauen in den Dörfern begleitet. Sie erhalten Informationen zur Schwangerschaft und Risiken, sicheren Entbindung, Ernährung und Hygiene. Über die Programme konnte erreicht werden, dass mittlerweile 99% der Frauen des Einzugsgebiets während der Schwangerschaft medizinisch betreut werden und 39% der Frauen in Bushulo entbinden. In Zusammenarbeit mit der Diözese Hawassa, der Caritas Auslandshilfe in Vorarlberg und dem langjährigen ehrenamtlichen Engagement von Dr. Bruno und Marlene Renner aus Frastanz ist es in dieser Region, die flächenmäßig rund 101.000 km2 groß ist, in den vergangenen Jahren gelungen, den medizinischen Standard von elf kleinen Ambulanzen, die die Diözese Hawassa vorwiegend in abgelegenen Regionen unterhält, sukzessive zu verbessern. Zudem wurde das Gesundheitszentrum Bushulo, nahe der Stadt Hawassa gelegen, in eine Mutter-Kind-Spezialklinik umgebaut- ein Pionierprojekt für die ganze Region. Dabei reicht das Spektrum der erforderlichen medizinischen Versorgung von der Betreuung der Mütter während der Schwangerschaft (u.a. Der Neubau mit 69 Betten und professionell ausgestatteten Operations- und Geburtsräumen wird Ende 2020 fertig gestellt. Die neue Spezialklinik ist dann das erste und einzige Spezialzentrum für Mutter-Kind-Gesundheit in ganz Südäthiopien und soll künftig professionelle Dienstleitungen in den Bereichen Geburtshilfe, Gynäkologie und Pädiatrie anbieten. title: A MAGICAL SATURDAY AT CCF26: COLNAGO GRAVEL, FAMILY, AND CONAD JUNIOR BIKE
description: – The Queen of the Festival starts tomorrow at 7:30 a.m. Saturday at the Colnago Lake Garda Cycling Festival was a whirlwind of excitement, filled with sports, fun, and solidarity. The day began at 9:30 a.m., when Desenzano del Garda welcomed the participants of the Colnago Gravel “Terra del Garda” , who rode 63 km or 38 km through the spectacular scenery of the Brescia side of Lake Garda. The cyclists made their first stop in Salò , at Piazza Baden Powell, where they refueled with a hearty meal to continue the ride in top form! They then crossed the finish line in Padenghe sul Garda , at Palazzo Barbieri, the town hall. A grand closing celebration full of surprises awaited them at the finish line, featuring products from the Strada dei Vini del Garda and the presence of reenactors from the “Padenghe Tricolore.” In the afternoon, downtown Desenzano became the scene of a wonderful celebration! Starting at 2:00 PM, the first cyclists brought Piazza Malvezzi to life, where the race packs and bib numbers for the Granfondo Colnago were handed out. At 2:30 PM, the second edition of the CONAD Junior Bike took place, an event designed for young athletes who gathered on the Cesare Battisti Lakeside Promenade to tackle skill challenges on their bikes—this year’s sole round of the Regional Championship . At the end of the event, all participants were treated to a tasty CONAD snack, followed by the dedicated awards ceremony. Meanwhile, children and parents took their places at the starting line for the Colnago Family ride, a guided tour led by the Garda Cycling Academy and designed for parents and children of all ages. The Colnago Family ride symbolized the union of sports and solidarity: all proceeds from event registration will be donated to the Ronald McDonald House in Brescia . A special thank you goes to all our partners—X-BIONIC, Ekoi, Tomasi Auto, Noleggiare, and Named—who brought life and color to the day in the Festival’s Expo area. At 7:30 p.m., the official start of the second edition of Desenzano By Night took place, a 3- and 6-kilometer recreational walk to admire the views of Lake Garda at sunset. To wrap up the day, the CCF organizers treated participants and guests of the Colnago Lake Garda Cycling Festival to a fireworks display over the lake . At the end of this beautiful and exciting day, all that remains is to thank all the participants, as we look forward to the highlight of the festival, the Granfondo Colnago , tomorrow morning.

Working within a multidisciplinary team, the Physiotherapist facilitates functional recovery, promotes independence, optimizes prosthetic use, and improves patients’ quality of life through evidence-based rehabilitation practices The Physiotherapist tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following points: Undertake a comprehensive and accurate assessment of patients in a variety of settings; Identify, plan and manage physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation plans Provide physio treatments to achieve identified outcomes and monitor patients’ conditions, both for in-patients and out-patients, if needed; Perform all the tasks related to the physio competence framework; Establish, maintain and conclude therapeutic interpersonal relationships with patients and their relatives, based on respect, dignity and care; Conduct comprehensive physical assessments of patients with upper and lower limb amputations, including musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, balance, gait, and functional evaluations. Provide pre-prosthetic rehabilitation, including: residual limb care and shaping, edema management, scar management, pain management (including phantom limb pain where appropriate), range of motion and strengthening exercises, contracture prevention Cardiovascular conditioning Deliver prosthetic rehabilitation, including: prosthetic gait training, balance and coordination training, functional mobility training Stair negotiation and community ambulation Transfers and activities of daily living (ADL) training Fall prevention strategies Monitor patient progress and modify treatment plans according to clinical outcomes. Encourage patients to have a positive attitude towards physiotherapy by motivating them; Organizing daily group activities, if possible, for patients; Promote an environment that enables patient’s safety and health implementing all necessary actions such as infection control practices, bed sores prevention practices and maintaining high level of hygiene also ensuring physio material are properly cleaned; Ensure that the equipment is functional and well maintained and stored; Ensure documentation/record is accurate and physio chart is properly filled, maintaining confidentially of information; Compiling and submitting periodic reports, if requested, following EMERGENCY guidelines; Be compliant with EMERGENCY guidelines for the treatment of patients; Work closely with prosthetists/orthotists during prosthetic prescription, fitting, alignment, and follow-up. Provide clinical feedback regarding prosthetic fit, function, comfort, and patient performance. Participate in training programs or activities, meeting timelines and deliverables, if requested by EMERGENCY; Train new staff, if needed. Job requirements: Degree in the Physio field; (Bachelor’s Degree in Physiotherapy from a recognized institution). Postgraduate training in rehabilitation, prosthetics, amputee rehabilitation, or neurorehabilitation Experience working in prosthetic and orthotic services. Good problem solving, time management and technical skills and willingness to learn new procedures and techniques; Good communication, interpersonal skills and high level of empathy, patience and ability to handle emotional and pressure situations; Basic Computer Skills, including Microsoft Office Program; Good level of English, written and spoken.

The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our programs are primarily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work. Vital Strategies is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive (DEI) organization. We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences, whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Lead Poisoning Prevention Program: Vital Strategies is expanding our program that addresses the issue of lead poisoning in low- and middle-income countries. We plan to build upon existing efforts and interest by collaborating with governmental agencies in countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to strengthen health systems and build local expertise in childhood lead exposure to enact sound, cost-effective policies to address exposures. Job Purpose: The position of Government Relations Advisor, Africa will facilitate regional exchange and coordinate high-level engagement and partnership building for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program across multiple countries in Africa. The role will focus on managing and strengthening relationships with key government and program partners, stakeholders, facilitating regional exchanges and strategy development, and ensuring program alignment with countries’ priorities and global objectives. The incumbent will work closely with country teams to support government engagement, partnership building, share updates on implementation progress, and ensure exchange and coordination among government and consortium partners across the regional portfolio. The role will also provide representation at regional events, support policy engagement, and ensure effective collaboration among regional stakeholders and technical partners. It is preferred that this role be based in Ethiopia, on a full-time hybrid schedule, out of Vital Strategies' office in Addis Ababa, but we are also open to qualified candidates from Ghana, Rwanda, and Tanzania. The candidate must have authorization to work legally in the respective country at the time of hire. Vital Strategies offers highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position will vary by location, experience and qualifications. Partnership Management - · Support country teams in managing key government and institutional partners across the region, as well as non-government organizations in relevant sectors; · Represent Vital Strategies in regional lead poisoning prevention meetings, technical forums, public hearings, and governance bodies in the region; · Support the development and review of reports, policy briefs, and training materials developed in the region; · Promote cross-sector dialogues that support the development of integrated, evidence-based public policies; · Facilitate knowledge exchange across the region; · Coordinate work with national and international partners, ensuring alignment across local and global strategies; · Assist with other duties as specified by the supervisor. Procurement Summary

Item                                      Description 

Client                                      Girl Effect Ethiopia 

Assignment                         Prequalification of Printing, Branding & Production Service Providers

Procurement Method     Open Competitive Procurement                                        

Contract Type                     Framework Agreement                                                   

Framework Period            September 2026 – August 2028                                      

Number of Suppliers       Multiple suppliers may be appointed                             

Location                                 Ethiopia                                                           

Currency                                Ethiopian Birr (ETB)                                           

Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organisation that creates media, technology and behaviour change programmes that empower adolescent girls and young people to improve their health, education and economic opportunities.

In Ethiopia, Girl Effect delivers programmes through the Yegna youth brand, reaching millions of young people through media, digital platforms, community engagement and research. These programmes require a wide range of professionally produced printing, branding and promotional materials to support programme implementation across Ethiopia

Objective

Girl Effect Ethiopia seeks to establish a roster of qualified printing, branding and production service providers for a two-year Framework Agreement.

Suppliers appointed to the framework may be invited to participate in:

  • Restricted Requests for Quotations (RFQs)
  • Mini-competitions
  • Direct call-off assignments

depending on the nature, value and complexity of future requirements.

Appointment to the framework does not guarantee any minimum volume of work.

Framework Period

The framework agreement shall remain valid for:

September  2026 –August 2028

Girl Effect reserves the right to extend the framework for an additional period, subject to satisfactory performance.

What You’ll Do

The selected suppliers shall be capable of providing one or more of the following services:

A. Programme and Educational Materials

Student Manuals /Facilitator Guides  – Booklets - 60 pages

  • Size: A5  Portrait (unless otherwise specified)
  • Printing: Full colour (CMYK), double-sided
  • Inside Pages: 150 GSM white bond paper, glossy
  • Cover: 300 gsm art card with matte or gloss lamination
  • Binding: Saddle stitched or perfect bound depending on page count
  • Finish: Trimmed and neatly finished

Discussion Guides – Flip Charts - 20 pages

  • Size: A3 Landscape (297 × 420 mm)
  • Printing: Full colour, double-sided
  • Paper: 250 gsm art card, glossy
  • Mounting: White laminated rigid board backing
  • Type: Self-standing flip chart
  • Finish: Durable and suitable for repeated use during training sessions

Conversation Card - Flash Cards

  • Size: A5 or A6 (as specified)
  • Printing: Full colour, double-sided
  • Material: 300 gsm art card
  • Finish: Matte or gloss lamination with rounded corners where required

Fact Sheets - Brochure

  • Size: A4 or A3 folded
  • Printing: Full colour, double-sided
  • Paper: 170 gsm art paper
  • Finish: Folded and neatly trimmed

B. Information, Education and Communication Materials

Posters

  • Sizes: A3, A2, A1 or custom sizes
  • Printing: Full colour, single or double-sided
  • Paper: 200 gsm art paper
  • Finish: Matte or gloss finish as required

Flyers

  • Printing: Full colour, double-sided
  • Paper: 150 gsm art paper
  • Finish: Trimmed and bundled

Leaflets

  • Printing: Full colour
  • Paper: 150–170 gsm art paper
  • Finish: Bi-fold or tri-fold as required

Brochures

  • Size: A4 folded (Bi-fold or Tri-fold)
  • Printing: Full colour
  • Paper: 170 gsm art paper
  • Finish: Professionally folded

Calendars

  • Printing: Full colour
  • Cover: 300 gsm art card
  • Inside Pages: 170–200 gsm art paper
  • Binding: Wire binding with hanging hook where applicable

Stickers

  • Printing: Full colour
  • Finish: Gloss laminated
  • Cutting: Die-cut or kiss-cut depending on design

  • Printing: Full colour
  • Includes: Aluminium stand and carrying bag

  • Printing: Full colour

  • Printing: Single or full colour
  • Paper: 100–120 gsm bond paper

Note: Suppliers should demonstrate capability to print materials in: Amharic, Afan Oromo,  Sidamic, Afar, Somali, Tigrinya, English and other Ethiopian languages where required.

Procurement Timelines

  • Terms of Reference Published: July  29, 2026
  • Deadline for Proposal Submission: August 20, 2026

Supplier Eligibility Requirements

Interested suppliers must submit:

Company Documentation

  • Valid Business License

  • Certificate of Incorporation/Registration

  • TIN Registration Certificate

  • VAT Registration Certificate

  • Valid Tax Clearance Certificate

  • Company Profile

Technical Capacity

  • Description of printing facilities

  • List of printing equipment

  • List of finishing equipment

  • Production capacity per day/week

  • Quality assurance procedures

Relevant Experience

  • Minimum three years experience providing printing services

  • At least three references from similar assignments

  • Portfolio of completed work

Financial Capacity

  • Audited financial statements (last two years) or equivalent financial records

  • Bank reference letter

Proposal Submission Requirements

Technical Proposal

The technical proposal should include:

Company Overview

  • Company profile

  • Years in operation

  • Areas of specialization

Relevant Experience

  • Similar assignments undertaken

  • NGO, donor or development sector experience

Production Capacity

  • Printing technology available

  • Production capability

  • Staffing structure

Quality Management

  • Quality assurance processes

  • Sample approval procedures

  • Reprint and defect management processes

Delivery and Logistics

  • Delivery capability

  • Geographic coverage

  • Turnaround times

Sample Submission

Suppliers should submit at least three examples of recently completed print assignments demonstrating:

  • Colour quality

  • Binding quality

  • Finishing quality

  • Branding execution

  • Durability

Financial Proposal

The Financial Proposal in Ethiopian shall be submitted separately from the Technical Proposal using the Girl Effect Pricing Schedule.

The Pricing Schedule has been designed to ensure a consistent and comparable evaluation of all submissions. Suppliers are requested to complete all applicable sections of the template and return it in its original Excel format.

The completed pricing schedule should include, where applicable:

  • Unit rates for all requested printing and production items.

  • VAT and other applicable taxes.

  • Delivery and transportation charges.

  • Installation costs (where applicable).

  • Minimum order quantities (where applicable).

  • Standard production lead times.

  • Bulk order discounts.

  • Any additional charges or assumptions.

  • Price validity period.

Where a particular item or service is not offered, suppliers should indicate "Not Applicable (N/A)" within the template rather than deleting rows.

Suppliers should not alter the structure or formulas contained within the pricing schedule unless specifically instructed by Girl Effect.

The completed Financial Proposal template should be submitted together with the Technical Proposal by the submission deadline.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Relevant Experience 25%
  • Technical Capacity 25%
  • Quality Assurance & Samples 20%
  • Delivery & Logistics Capability 10%
  • Financial Competitiveness 15%
  • References 5%

Framework Management

Girl Effect reserves the right to:

  • Appoint multiple suppliers to the framework.
  • Allocate suppliers by service category where appropriate.
  • Conduct restricted RFQs or mini-competitions amongst prequalified suppliers.
  • Issue direct call-off purchase orders where appropriate.
  • Review supplier performance annually.
  • Suspend or remove suppliers based on performance or compliance.
  • Extend the framework period subject to satisfactory performance.

How To Apply

To apply for this opportunity, please submit a proposal by email with the subject line “Prequalification of Printing, Branding and Production Service Providers – Ethiopia (2026–2028) ” to suppliers@girleffect.org  by August 20, 2026. For any questions, please also send them to our suppliers email address.

Commercial and General Terms

  • This procurement is intended to establish a non-exclusive framework agreement with multiple suppliers. Appointment to the framework does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work.
  • Suppliers are responsible for ensuring compliance with Ethiopian tax legislation. All taxes should be clearly identified in the financial proposal. 
  • All materials developed under any subsequent call-off assignment shall become the property of Girl Effect unless otherwise agreed in writing. 
  • Successful suppliers will be required to comply with Girl Effects safeguarding policies and may be required to undergo safeguarding checks before contract award. 
  • Girl Effect reserves the right to amend, suspend or cancel this procurement process at any stage and is not liable for any costs incurred by suppliers during the preparation or submission of proposals.

title: Ethiopia Innovations and Growth Lead
description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).
  • Experience identifying strategic gaps and designing "Learning Agendas" - knowing exactly which questions we need to answer through field trials before committing to a national-scale rollout.
  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred. 

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

On-site in Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, with regular visits to our field areas of operations (around 35% of the time).

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

 

Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

About our Internship Program

Join the One Acre Fund 2026 Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) Internship Program to jump-start your career. We empower you as you grow in this program which is especially designed for motivated young professionals.

When joining, you will participate in an onboarding program and receive training on how to accomplish your assigned projects. Over the period of your internship, you will also receive opportunities to learn directly from inspiring leaders to build foundations for your future career.

About the Role
